nodes.title: Managing State Schema Changes Across LangSmith Deployment Versions
openai-agents-python PR #4680: preserve writes that land while responses.compact is in flight
openai-agents-python issue #4775: RunState pending input duplicated when a Session append loses acknowledgement
openai-agents-python issue #6091: Runner.run with Session drops in-flight and completed sibling function_calls on cancellation
openai-agents-python issue #4988: OpenAIConversationsSession.pop_item is not safe for concurrent calls

nodes.text: Per-turn session persistence leaves a window where an external effect is committed but the session has no record of it: OpenAI Agents SDK issue #6091 reproduces a cancelled run whose external ledger holds both refunds while the Session holds only the user message, so a rerun cannot see the completed effect and may repeat it. Pydantic AI's step persistence states that an in-flight step is not retried and that tools with external effects need their own idempotency or reconciliation.
nodes.applicability: Cancellation and timeout mid-run in the OpenAI SDK; Pydantic AI statement concerns its step-persistence harness, which checkpoints per step (the candidate does not).
nodes.limitations: Issue #6091 is open with no maintainer reply; the Pydantic idempotency point is a paraphrase of the page, not a quoted sentence.

nodes.text: OpenAI Agents SDK issue #4775: if Session.add_items() commits and then raises (lost acknowledgement), a retried run appends the same logical input twice and reruns the input guardrail. A maintainer closed it as not establishing practical impact in a supported backend workflow, and said closure does not mean the code path was fixed.
nodes.limitations: Reproduced with a fake Session that stores then raises; a client-managed Session with RunState, not the built-in SQLite backend.

nodes.text: Pydantic AI durable execution: a tool run with durable=False executes in workflow code and runs again on every replay, and a restarted run replays completed units from the journal and retries the one in flight. Tools kept out of the durable unit must be deterministic.
nodes.applicability: Durable engines (Temporal/DBOS style) with journaled steps; not per-turn persistence.

nodes.text: A reproducible same-session overlap bug exists in the OpenAI Agents SDK: run_compaction, triggered after every turn save, could silently delete a concurrent add_items from an overlapping Runner.run on the same session. It was fixed by maintainer PR #4736, not by #4680 itself. Concurrent pop_item calls on OpenAIConversationsSession can also return the same item (#4988; closed, maintainer asked for a real-API scenario). The sessions docs add concurrency guarantees only for the compaction wrapper, none for plain sessions.
nodes.limitations: #4680 test plan uses event-gated interleavings, not a free-running repro; #4988 repro used a fake client. #4736 merge status taken from the #4680 page, not fetched. No equivalent report found for Pydantic AI or LangGraph OSS.

nodes.text: LangGraph's four multitask strategies for two runs on one thread (reject, enqueue as default, interrupt, rollback) are documented as a LangSmith Agent Server feature, not part of the open-source framework. Interrupt can leave a started-but-unfinished tool call that the graph must clean up.
nodes.applicability: LangSmith Agent Server; an embedded library has to implement its own policy.

nodes.text: Pydantic AI's harness guards a conversation head against concurrent writers: a stale writer or a deleted session raises ConversationConflict; SQLite writes wait up to 30 seconds for another writer; busy detection is local, not a distributed lease, and the database must not be shared between hosts. Single process is the supported scope.
nodes.limitations: Applies to the step-persistence harness stores; the plain message_history pattern has no such guard in the pages read.

nodes.text: Versioning of stored data differs by library. Pydantic AI step persistence: marker format is versioned, compatibility is upgrade-only, old SQLite DBs gain the new column on open. Pydantic message history is saved via ModelMessagesTypeAdapter and older histories need a load-time context flag (rebuild_unrecorded_tool_files) then a re-save. LangGraph: the latest graph applies to every thread; adding optional state fields is safe, while a type change, required field without default, or rename makes existing checkpoints fail or lose data. OpenAI Agents SDK sessions page documents no version or migration mechanism (SQLite rows are JSON; only the MongoDB backend notes legacy per-item documents remain readable).
nodes.limitations: Documentation of rules, not bug reports. The OpenAI claim rests on absence from a docs page and is inference-grade.

nodes.text: For a single-process library saving once per completed turn, the stored-history format should carry a version marker and a tolerant reader (optional new fields, upgrade-only reads, re-save after load), as Pydantic AI does, because LangGraph documents that type changes, required fields without defaults and renames break existing checkpoints.

What does the official LangGraph durable-execution page (docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/durable-execution) say verbatim about wrapping side effects in tasks and idempotency? The fetch returned other pages in this run, so only secondary summaries were seen.
